item.title: Gaps on supermarket shelves believed to be result of weather disruptions
item.description: Fresh produce and some meat products were in short supply at several outlets

item.title: WATCH | Ian Borg defends Malta’s cautious approach on Trump’s Greenland rhetoric
item.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ian Borg questions whether Malta should be presumptuous enough to issue an early standalone statement on US President Donald Trump’s rhetoric on Greenland, saying it is an issue which primarily concerns NATO countries

item.title: Man who allegedly left wife, daughter with black-eye in domestic abuse dispute gets bail
item.description: Man accused of domestic violence against his wife and one of his daughters granted bail, with the court issuing a protection order

item.description: Two of the individuals seen driving recklessly are just 18 years old, while another two are 21-year-olds,

item.title: Court accepts victim’s decision to drop domestic violence case

item.title: Standards Committee votes down further action against Alex Borg over Fort Chambray lie
item.description: During the session, the committee also voted on two other cases surrounding the use of public funds for adverts belonging to Education Minister Clifton Grima and Prime Minister Robert Abela. No action will be taken against anyone involved in all cases

item.title: WATCH | PL deputy leader plays down Jason Micallef’s cryptic post on the hand that will bite back
item.description: Labour Deputy Leader Alex Agius Saliba says he did not discuss cryptic social media posts made in recent days by Ta’ Qali National Park chairman Jason Micallef, defending him for the ‘great work’ he has done in his various government roles

item.title: Police looking for missing woman
item.description: Jessica Farrugia was last seen in Ħamrun wearing blue jeans, white shoes, and a brown top

item.title: Alleged trafficking victim describes living in fear, being fed once daily while living in brothel
item.description: A Venezuelan woman testifies that she intended to work in Malta for only two weeks, describing strict rules, financial control and degrading living conditions inside a St Julian’s brothel
